perf.summary: Init takes 'ptr' and 's' parameters that are never used; drop them.
perf.currentCost: Dead parameters 'int* ptr' and 'int s' (line 9) force callers to pass and the ABI to pass extra register/stack slots; they also mislead readers about what the function touches.
perf.proposedChange: Change signature to Init(int n, int* head, int* currentArc) and update callers. Loop body only uses head and currentArc.
perf.rationale: Fewer argument slots per call (this is AggressiveInlining so likely free post-inline, but the signature clarity and avoidance of accidental aliasing assumptions matter). Pure cleanup.
perf.risk: Breaking signature change; must update all callers. Behavior identical.

perf.summary: Hoist level[u]+1 out of the scan loop and reorder the && so the cheaper level test still gates first but the invariant is precomputed.
perf.currentCost: level[u] (line 20) is reloaded and incremented on every edge probed in the current-arc scan; under pointers Burst cannot hoist it because flow/level writes elsewhere defeat alias analysis at the call boundary, and this is the hottest loop in Dinic.
perf.proposedChange: At entry compute 'int want = level[u] + 1;' once, then test 'if (level[v] == want && cap[e] - flow[e] > 0)'. u is fixed for the whole call.
perf.rationale: Removes a load+add from every edge examined across the entire Dinic DFS, which dominates runtime on dense layered graphs. Strict invariant: u does not change within Advance.
perf.risk: None; u is a by-value parameter, level[u] is not written inside Advance.
